question.problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

I. $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,3]$

II. $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$

III. $R=[-2,2]\times [-3,1]$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw our region $D:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14257924/assets/78af77d697ea292385e2bd2570c8185c728f57cc70c3edcc25ecccd0e84780e8.png)

Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given rectangles.

- Rectangles II and III do not cover the region $D.$

- Rectangle I cover the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
